en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} grew 14.0% between the last two censuses, against 5.2% nationally. That is the highest rate of any market on this site, and it has a consequence most consultants never mention: your account's history is a description of a city that no longer exists. The bid strategy trained on last year's conversions, the negative keyword list built two years ago, the assumption about which competitors matter, all of it decays faster in {city} than it would in Winnipeg or Halifax. Accounts here need re-examining on a schedule rather than left alone because they are performing.

Growth also means the competitive field keeps taking on new entrants who have no local reputation and therefore buy attention instead. If you have been in {city} for fifteen years, you are increasingly bidding against businesses with no word of mouth and a real budget, and your advantage has to be moved somewhere they cannot outspend, which usually means organic and AI visibility rather than the auction.

Then there is the season. {industries} here run on a summer peak that distorts every month-over-month comparison anyone shows you. A {city} account that looks like it is collapsing in October is often just a business in a city where October is quiet, and judging a channel on a thirty-day window across a seasonal boundary is how good campaigns get switched off for no reason.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account. If you want someone who will walk into your shop, I am the wrong hire and I will say so on the call rather than after you have paid.

faq.q: Our ads worked last year and stopped. What changed?
faq.a: In {city} the most common answer is that the market changed rather than the account. New competitors entered the auction, the customer base partly turned over, and a bid strategy trained on older data kept optimising toward a pattern that had already gone. It is worth checking the seasonal boundary too, because a summer-to-autumn comparison here flatters and then punishes almost every business in town.

faq.q: Should we target {city} or the whole Okanagan?
faq.a: Depends whether people will drive to you. For most services the valley is one market and restricting to the city limits leaves real customers out. For anything where the customer expects you to come to them, a tight radius is correct and widening it just buys you clicks you cannot serve.

faq.q: How do we compete with a new competitor outspending us?
faq.a: Usually not in the auction, because if their whole plan is to buy attention they will pay more per click than the maths justifies and you should let them. The durable answer is to own the organic result and the AI recommendation, both of which reward the years you have been here and cannot be bought in a quarter.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
